mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M260 engine for an A35 AMG typically costs between £1,200 and £7,800 depending on condition. Used units start from £1,200-£2,500, reconditioned from £2,800-£5,000, and fully rebuilt from £3,800-£7,800. A replacement M260.920 engine costs on average £5,834 in good condition, with new or reconditioned engines costing up to £7,779. Labour for supply & fit adds £600-£1,000 for AMG-specialist work.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The A35 AMG uses the M260 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. However, the M260 is known for timing chain tensioner wear - a rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign. Mercedes has issued a TSB (08.02.16) for this issue, with an updated tensioner part (A2600502000) available.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the A35 AMG include: a rattling noise on cold start (timing chain tensioner), misfires or rough running (cylinder head issues), excessive oil consumption or blue smoke from the exhaust (piston ring wear), and turbocharger lag or overheating. If you experience any of these, have the car inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A W177 A35 AMG is typically worth £15,000-£35,000 - a rebuilt M260 engine (£3,800-£7,800) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair (tensioner, cylinder head) may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M260 in the A35 AMG and the M260 in the A250?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the A35 AMG and A250 use the M260.920 2.0-litre turbo petrol engine, but with significantly different outputs. The A250 produces 224 hp, while the A35 AMG produces 306 hp - an 82 hp increase. The A35 AMG's M260 features a twin-scroll turbocharger, revised engine management, and AMG-specific calibration. Both share the same 83.0mm bore and 92.0mm stroke measurements.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG to misfire?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M260-equipped A35 AMG models, misfires are most commonly caused by cylinder head deformation allowing combustion gases to leak. Faulty spark plugs, ignition coils, or clogged fuel injectors are also common culprits. Overseas owners have reported cylinder head leakage as a common issue on A35 models, with some markets seeing extended warranties offered for this problem.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A35 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The A35 AMG arrived with the fourth-generation W177 A-Class in 2018 as the entry-level model from Mercedes-AMG. It introduced a revised version of the M260 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine, described by AMG as a "new development" that shares its 83.0mm bore and 92.0mm stroke measurements with the M133 engine of the A45 AMG. The A35 AMG was positioned to bridge the gap between the standard A-Class and the flagship A45, offering 306 hp and a 0-62 mph time of 4.7 seconds.

milestones.description: M260.920, 2.0L turbo petrol, 306 hp (225 kW) - W177 A35 AMG launch; twin-scroll turbocharger; 400 Nm torque; 7-speed AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT; 0-62 mph in 4.7 seconds

48V mild-hybrid assistance added to some markets; +14 hp electric boost

problems.h4: M260 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the A35 AMG Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M260 engine suffers from timing chain tensioner wear, with a Mercedes TSB (08.02.16) identifying this as a known issue. Harmonics from the timing chain drive can cause the tensioner to lose pressure, leading to a rattling noise on startup. If left unchecked, the timing chain can skip, causing piston-to-valve contact.

For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M260 with warranty (£3,800-£7,800) offers peace of mind. The A35 AMG's strong retained values mean replacement is usually justified for well-maintained cars.

problems.h4: M260 Cylinder Head Failure - A35 AMG Misfires and Rough Running
problems.rootCause: The M260 engine can suffer from cylinder head deformation, allowing combustion gases to leak past the cylinder head gasket. This is a known issue on A35 and A35L models, with overseas owners reporting that cylinder head leakage is a common problem. Fault codes related to misfires, particularly on cylinder 2 or 3, are common indicators.
